newsitem.title: USA: Black man pleads guilty in Texas church fire.
newsitem.headline: Black man pleads guilty in Texas church fire.

text.p: An 18-year-old African-American man pleaded guilty on Monday to arson in the June 1996 fire at the predominantly black Church of the Living God in Greenville, Texas, federal prosecutors said.
Mark Anthony Young, who has been in custody since his arrest July 22, 1966, was sentenced to time served in jail and three years probation, First Assistant U.S. Attorney Richard Stephens said.
Young pleaded guilty to one count of arson, and a second count was dismissed in the case. The plea agreement and investigative reports were sealed in the case, prosecutors said.
After he was arrested Young confessed to setting the blaze that damaged the church and also admitted to burning down several vacant houses around Greenville, just outside Dallas, prosecutors said.
The church burning was part of a series of Southern church fires over the past two years that sparked racial tensions and an investigation by the Justice Department Civil Rights Division.
